$no_roadmap_note: ROADMAP.md is deliberately ABSENT from this list, and must not be re-added (ANTS-4529). It is generated from the roadmap store by RoadmapRender::render(), which replays the root section's stored intro verbatim — so a pattern/replace edit to the markdown is discarded by the next roadmap_log write of ANY op, silently, at whatever later moment someone appends a bullet. It fired four times in one session on 2026-08-19. The banner no longer carries a version at all: the number was a duplicate of CMakeLists.txt's project(VERSION), and the sentence holding it already links CHANGELOG.md, which carries every shipped version, dated. Locked by tests/features/bump_recipe_no_generated_files/.
$tag_note: Annotated tag created + pushed by the /release skill (step 9) after the release commit lands on origin/main. Distro packagers resolve v{NEW} back to a tarball via GitHub's /archive/refs/tags/v{NEW}.tar.gz URL — the openSUSE spec and Arch PKGBUILD's Source0 line depends on the tag existing.
$todos_run_before_post_check: All entries below MUST be done BEFORE running `post_check`. The drift script flags packaging/linux/za.co.antsprojectshub.AntsTerminal.metainfo.xml and packaging/debian/changelog because their version-bearing lines live inside the per-release blocks the recipe can't auto-generate — so the bump skill must hand off these todos and only then re-run post_check to confirm clean.
todos: **On minor or major bumps only (not patch):** rotate the just-closed minor's section out of ROADMAP.md into docs/roadmap/<closed>.md by running `bash packaging/rotate-roadmap.sh <closed-minor>`. ANTS-1125 / spec INV-14. Skipped on patch bumps because per-patch sections aren't supported (per-minor only). The script is idempotent on an already-rotated roadmap.

**Do NOT author a CHANGELOG.md section — leave the file alone.** `packaging/cut-rc.sh new-rc` rolls `## [Unreleased]` into `## [{NEW}] — unreleased (Patron RC preview)` right after this bump, and `promote` date-stamps that heading on release day. Two reasons this todo used to say the opposite and was wrong on both: (a) `roll_unreleased` is a NO-OP against a target section that already has content (cut-rc.sh, the `treal` branch), so authoring one here strands the whole cycle's entries in `[Unreleased]` and ships an RC whose notes are empty; (b) it claimed to be 'required for post_check to pass', but `check-version-drift.sh` does not inspect CHANGELOG.md at all — only the spec, PKGBUILD, debian changelog, man page, metainfo, README and ROADMAP. Corrected 2026-08-13 during the 0.7.104→0.7.105 cycle. Entries reach `[Unreleased]` as work lands, via `mcp__ants__changelog_log` — not at bump time.

Prepend a new `ants-terminal ({NEW}-1) unstable; urgency=medium` block to packaging/debian/changelog with body bullets and `-- Anthony Schemel <aant.schemel@gmail.com>  <RFC2822 date>` footer. **Required for post_check to pass.** Use `dch -v {NEW}-1` if you want the boilerplate (date, header line) formatted automatically.

**README.md content check (not just its version banner).** The banner is bumped automatically by the `files` list above; this todo is about the PROSE going stale. Read README.md against what actually shipped this cycle and update it ONLY if a user-visible claim has drifted — do not touch it otherwise, an unchanged README is the normal outcome. The claims that go stale, in order of likelihood: (a) the built-in-tool COUNT ("87 ready-made tools") — verify with `tool_info {catalog:true}` and read `tool_count`; it drifted 58 -> 87 unnoticed before this todo existed; (b) the theme count and scrollback ceiling in the Settings table; (c) the Install section, if a new distro package or store listing went live; (d) any feature bullet describing behaviour a release changed, and any opt-in feature that changed its default. A count is the highest-risk kind of claim here because nothing else in the build verifies it.

**Check the roadmap store for shipped-but-unrecorded work** — run `bash tools/check-shipped-coverage.sh`. It reads the store's `shipped` dates and lists every item closed since the last public tag that no CHANGELOG bullet cites. This is the CONVERSE of cut-release Phase 0f, which only checks that ids the CHANGELOG claims are really shipped — nothing checked the other direction until ANTS-4714, and the first run found 19 uncovered items, one of them closed the same day by the session cutting the release. Run it HERE, before `new-rc` rolls `[Unreleased]`: afterwards a missing entry has to go into a closed section instead of the open one. Each hit is either release-note-worthy (add it with `changelog_log`) or deliberately internal — say which in the release report rather than leaving it looking like an oversight. The gate skips loudly when it cannot see (no sqlite3, no store, unregistered project, no public tag) and always reports how many shipped items carry no date and were therefore invisible to it.
After todos 1-3 are written, run post_check (`bash packaging/check-version-drift.sh`) and confirm exit 0 before proceeding to build/test/commit.
Run `cd build && cmake --build . --parallel && ctest --output-on-failure` to verify nothing broke.
